I have been farming this same land for decades. Quzhou is flat, good soil, and I know every corner of my 8 mu. My wife and I are just two people now, so I cannot take on too much extra work. I rely on what has worked year after year.

**Wheat (October planting, June harvest):**
I plant wheat every year on all 8 mu. I have used the same improved variety from the county seed station for years — Jimai series. I trust it. I will apply fertilizer in two splits: base fertilizer before planting, then urea top-dress at jointing. I water three times — once before winter freeze-up to protect the roots, once at jointing, once at heading. Two sprays: one herbicide early, one fungicide spray in April for powdery mildew. I use rotary tillage after maize is harvested to break up the stalks and loosen the soil.

**Maize (June planting, October harvest):**
Right after wheat harvest, I plant maize directly without plowing — no-tillage saves my back and keeps moisture. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, which my neighbors also use and which yields well here. Summer has enough rain most years, so I only irrigate once at tasseling if it is dry. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea at the big bell stage. One pesticide spray for corn borer if I see damage.

At 68, I keep things simple. I do not chase new technologies. I do what I know.
